scenario_description: US Treasury trade with quantity (face value) mismatch. High exposure due to notional size.
business_context: Institutional Treasury purchase. Large notional. Face value discrepancy creates significant settlement risk.

ground_truth.recommended_action: Escalate face value discrepancy to trading desk immediately. Do not settle. $5M face value difference creates $4.86M exposure at current price.

reviewer_notes: High-severity quantity break. Exposure = 5,000,000 × 0.97125 = $4,856,250. Tests severity classification — must be flagged as high impact, not routine.

scenario_description: ES futures trade with settlement date mismatch. Counterparty shows next-day settlement; internal shows same-day.
business_context: CME E-mini S&P 500 futures. Standard margin-based settlement. Date discrepancy affects margin calculation timing.

ground_truth.recommended_action: Verify settlement convention with clearing broker. CME futures settle same-day (T+0) for variation margin. Internal record appears correct. Request counterparty to amend.

reviewer_notes: Tests knowledge of futures settlement conventions. CME futures use T+0 variation margin settlement. The counterparty's T+1 date is likely incorrect. Moderate difficulty because the model must understand the convention to assess which side is right.

scenario_description: Listed equity option with commission discrepancy masked by correct pricing on all other fields.
business_context: CBOE-listed call option. All economic fields match. Commission rate differs between counterparty and internal records.

ground_truth.recommended_action: Flag commission discrepancy. Verify agreed commission rate with broker. Total difference: $30.00 (200 contracts × $0.15).

reviewer_notes: Tests attention to non-price fields. All economic fields match — the commission is the only discrepancy. Moderate difficulty because the model must not be distracted by the matching option-specific fields.

scenario_description: Vanilla IRS with counterparty mismatch and a subtle fixed rate difference. Two simultaneous exceptions.
business_context: SOFR-based IRS. 5-year tenor. Counterparty name on confirmation does not match internal record, and fixed rate differs by 0.5 basis points. Both must be identified.

ground_truth.recommended_action: Escalate immediately. Two exceptions: (1) Counterparty legal entity mismatch — may affect netting, ISDA master agreement, and regulatory reporting. Verify correct booking entity. (2) Fixed rate differs by 0.5 bps on $50M notional. Both must be resolved before confirmation. Do not proceed until legal entity is confirmed.

reviewer_notes: Complex case: two simultaneous exceptions. The counterparty mismatch is between related entities (LLC vs Inc) — model must flag this as a legal entity issue, not dismiss as a formatting difference. The 0.5 bps rate difference is subtle but material on $50M notional. Approximate exposure from rate break: $50M × 0.005% × 5 years ≈ $12,500. Model must identify both.

scenario_description: FX forward with currency pair correctly stated but settlement instructions pointing to the wrong nostro account.
business_context: EUR/USD 1-month forward. Economic terms match. Settlement instructions on the EUR leg reference an incorrect nostro account. This would result in failed delivery.

counterparty_confirmation.eur_settlement: Correspondent Bank X / SWIFT: COBADEFF / Account: DE89370400440532013000

internal_record.eur_settlement: Correspondent Bank Y / SWIFT: DEUTDEFF / Account: DE27100777770209299700

primary_exception.difference: Different correspondent bank, SWIFT code, and account number for EUR leg

ground_truth.recommended_action: Escalate SSI mismatch on EUR leg immediately. Incorrect settlement instructions will result in failed EUR delivery on $10.85M equivalent. Verify correct EUR nostro account with treasury and counterparty before settlement date.

reviewer_notes: SSI mismatches are among the most dangerous exceptions in FX — they result in failed deliveries. All economic terms match, so the model must look beyond price/quantity to catch the settlement instruction discrepancy. Severity 4 because the full notional is at risk.

scenario_description: CDS trade with booking discrepancy — trade booked to wrong legal entity internally. Counterparty confirmation is correct.
business_context: 5-year CDS on IG corporate reference entity. All economic terms match counterparty confirmation. Internal record shows trade booked under the wrong fund entity, which is not party to the ISDA with this counterparty.

primary_exception.counterparty_value: Trade with Dealer Bank Delta under ISDA with Fund A LP
primary_exception.internal_value: Booked to Fund B LP (no ISDA with Dealer Bank Delta)
primary_exception.difference: Internal booking entity (Fund B LP) is not the entity on the ISDA master agreement (Fund A LP)

ground_truth.recommended_action: Critical exception. Trade booked to Fund B LP but ISDA master agreement with Dealer Bank Delta is under Fund A LP. This trade has no legal basis under Fund B's documentation. Escalate immediately to legal, documentation, and operations. Rebook to correct entity (Fund A LP) or establish ISDA between Fund B LP and Dealer Bank Delta before settlement.
ground_truth.escalation_target: Legal, documentation, operations supervisor, portfolio manager

reviewer_notes: Critical-severity case. All economic terms match — the exception is in the booking entity vs. ISDA relationship. Model must recognize that 'account: FUND-B-CREDIT' and 'legal_entity: Fund B LP' conflicts with 'isda_entity: Fund A LP'. This requires understanding that trades must be booked under the entity that has an ISDA with the counterparty. Severity 5 because a CDS under no valid ISDA creates legal and regulatory exposure.

scenario_description: Equity trade where counterparty shows a different account allocation than internal record. Allocation discrepancy.
business_context: Block trade allocated across two accounts. Counterparty shows full allocation to one account; internal shows split allocation. Total quantity matches.

primary_exception.difference: Allocation split mismatch. Total quantity agrees (8,000). Distribution differs.

ground_truth.recommended_action: Allocation discrepancy. Total quantity matches (8,000 shares) but distribution across accounts differs. Verify correct allocation with portfolio manager and send updated allocation instructions to counterparty.

reviewer_notes: Tests ability to compare structured allocation arrays, not just scalar fields. Total quantity matches — the model must not dismiss this as a clean match. The discrepancy is in the allocation split, not the aggregate.

scenario_description: Corporate bond trade with clean economic match but duplicate confirmation — counterparty has sent the same confirmation twice with different timestamps.
business_context: IG corporate bond purchase. Economic terms match internal record. However, the counterparty has transmitted two confirmations for the same trade ID. The model must flag the duplicate rather than simply confirming the match.

counterparty_confirmation.confirmation_note: Second confirmation received for same trade ID

ground_truth.recommended_action: Duplicate confirmation detected. Economic terms match on both confirmations and match internal record. Investigate whether duplicate represents: (1) retransmission by counterparty, (2) amendment attempt, or (3) system error. Confirm with counterparty that only one trade was intended. Do not process second confirmation as a new trade.

reviewer_notes: Complex case. All economic fields match — a naive field-by-field comparison would mark this as clean. The exception is the duplicate confirmation indicator. The model must read the confirmation_count and confirmation_timestamps fields and recognize that receiving two confirmations for one trade ID is itself an exception, even when the content matches. Tests whether the model looks beyond economic terms.
references: Corporate bond T+2 settlement (transitioning to T+1)
